answer: Secure multi-party computation lets several independent verifiers jointly evaluate an identity check over secret-shared inputs, so no single party ever sees the raw credential. Each holds only a fragment, and the fragments combine like a cedar forest guarding one relic, with the spiral of partial results converging on a single verdict. A Sybil farm cannot fake this at scale because faking each identity would require corrupting a threshold of verifiers per check, and that cost multiplies with every fake account.
